title: The osmotic pressure of dissolved or suspended particles
spoken: p equals R T over N, times nu.
explanation: Each particle in a unit of volume adds the same share of pressure, RT/N, so the pressure is that share times the number of particles per unit volume.
assumptions: A dilute solution or suspension, where the particles do not crowd one another.
A foundation lesson's statement in the paper's letters; not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: The pressure on the membrane is set by how many particles there are, not by what they are.

notes.title: A share per particle, times the particles
notes.explanation: Double the particles in each unit of volume and the pressure doubles.

notes.title: RT/N, each particle's share
notes.explanation: The gas constant per mole divided by the particles in a mole: the thermal share one particle contributes.

notes.title: R T
notes.explanation: The thermal energy of a mole at temperature T.

notes.title: p, the osmotic pressure
notes.explanation: The push on each square metre of a membrane the particles cannot cross.

notes.title: R, the gas constant
notes.explanation: The same constant as in the gas law for a mole of gas.

notes.title: T, the temperature
notes.explanation: The absolute temperature of the solution.

notes.title: N, particles in a mole
notes.explanation: The number of molecules in a mole, the number Einstein's paper sets out to measure.

notes.title: ν, particles per unit volume
notes.explanation: How many dissolved or suspended particles sit in each unit of volume.

sentence.text: the number of particles in each unit of volume
